section_plan.title: Objective
content_bullets: Develop novel deep learning methods enabling neural networks to generalize across diverse physical environments and boundary conditions in physics domains
Address gaps in applying DL to physics problems where standard computer vision techniques fail
Demonstrate utility on three Navy-relevant physics tasks: underwater acoustics, RF propagation, and structural health monitoring
notebook_topics: differences between CV/NLP and physics applications

section_plan.title: Motivation and Background
content_bullets: Neural networks excel in CV/NLP but struggle with physics domain generalization
Emerging field of Simulation Intelligence merges scientific computing with neural networks
Current NN solutions lack evidence of good test performance over entire range of physically realizable inputs
Gap: no prior studies on generalization in physics domains
citation_hints: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Chen et al.)
Physics Meets Machine Learning survey (Meng et al.)

section_plan.title: Research Hypotheses
content_bullets: H1: CV/NLP generalization methods will improve physics task generalization
H2: Physics equations, symmetry, and invariances can improve domain-specific generalization
Two technical challenges: identify cross-domain techniques (TC1) and derive domain-specific methods (TC2)
citation_hints: generalization measures (Jiang et al., Dziugaite et al.)

section_plan.title: Application Domains
content_bullets: Underwater acoustics: PALIS project for transmission loss prediction from ocean properties
Meteorology: RF propagation in atmosphere using COAMPS data
Structural health monitoring: MINC project for damage detection on naval platforms
All three domains involve Helmholtz wave equation solutions
notebook_topics: robotic gantry experimental setup for SHM
citation_hints: Lamb wave propagation in metallic structures

section_plan.title: Neural Operator Framework
content_bullets: Neural operators learn mappings between infinite-dimensional function spaces
Neumann Series Neural Operator (NSNO) selected for Helmholtz equation
NSNO achieves 60% error reduction vs standard FNO on 2D Helmholtz problems
Enables universal physics solvers requiring single training cycle across parameter spaces

section_plan.title: Methodology
content_bullets: Task 1: Establish baselines for three domains using existing implementations
Task 2: Investigate CV/NLP generalization properties (data augmentation, architecture, hyperparameters)
Task 3: Develop physics-informed generalization techniques (symmetries, invariances, novel loss functions)
Contrastive output augmentation loss: positive MSE term plus negative terms for non-matching outputs

section_plan.title: Underwater Acoustics Results
content_bullets: Approximate solutions (ray-traces) as secondary input channels improve TL generation quality
Ray-trace vectors perform equivalently to secondary channels with faster runtime
Cyclical generation (TL→SSP→TL) cannot reliably assess TL quality due to complexity asymmetry
Frequency-specific training vs multi-frequency training comparisons
notebook_topics: fRange experiments (50/200 Hz train, 100 Hz test)

section_plan.title: Meteorology Results
content_bullets: Modified refractivity prediction in marine atmospheric surface layer
Ducting phenomena modeling (sub-refraction, standard-refraction, super-refraction, trapping)
Propagation factor calculation across atmospheric domain
S-band (3 GHz) and X-band (10 GHz) frequency experiments
notebook_topics: Eastern Mediterranean and Persian Gulf datasets

section_plan.title: Structural Health Monitoring Results
content_bullets: 100% detection accuracy achieved using Gabor representation of time-series wavepackets
Simulated damage via contact loads enables large experimental datasets
Automated robotic gantry generates tens of thousands of labeled training samples
Physics-first approach: neural networks leverage time-frequency sensor data directly
notebook_topics: convolutional layers for local feature extraction
